title: Midnight triage dry-run notes (customer-facing escalation)
content:
Purpose:
- Quick dry-run of a nighttime escalation with the oncall rota + SE to practice comms, role handoffs, and the short customer update script. Scenario: Nimbus Health production inference timeouts -> 5xxs from model-serving (p95 latency 3.2s -> errors for sync calls).

High-level objective:
- Confirm who says what to customer, validate telemetry checklist, exercise fallback model routing, and capture post-call action items. Keep it <30m.

Call logistics (prep checklist):
- Join bridge: Zoom link (private) + Slack huddle fallback.
- Have the following tabs open before start: 
  1) Redwood Console -> model routes (Nimbus-prod, region-us-west)
  2) SLO dashboard (p95 latency, error rate, CPU/GPU util)
  3) Recent logs: stackdriver/ELK filter: service=model-serving, trace_id, request_id
  4) JIRA NIM-3421 ticket stub + incident timeline note draft
  5) Customer AM contact card + escalation phone (Ravi cell)
  6) Rollback/variant mapping doc (Confluence link above)

Roles (dry-run assignments):
- Incident Commander (IC): Iona (me) — run the call, make decisions, escalate to ENG leads
- Service Lead (model-serving): Maya — triage logs, propose remedy (hotfix/rollback)
- SRE / Infra: Omar — check node health, autoscaler, infra quotas
- Customer Comms / AM: Ravi — deliver customer updates, set expectations
- Scribe: placeholder (Ravi if not concurrently AM) — record timeline + action items

Opening script (30–60s):
- "Hi team — quick dry-run for a hypothetical Nimbus Health latency incident. Goal: validate comms + fallback. We will run through detection -> mitigation -> back-to-customer script. No live infra changes unless explicitly agreed. Notes captured in JIRA NIM-3421."

Triage flow (steps to practice):
1) Confirm symptom and scope: which endpoints, percent of requests failing, affected customers/tenants (is this only Nimbus?)
2) Correlate with infra: recent deployments, autoscale events, GPU OOMs, node churn, dmesg or kernel OOM logs
3) Apply quick mitigations (if live): 
   - temporary route split to variant with lower latency (model-xsmall)
   - enable aggressive prefix caching or TTL bump for embeddings
   - throttle or rate-limit heavy batch jobs to free capacity
4) If mitigation applied: monitor for p95 drop and error rate recovery for 10m window
5) If not recoverable: initiate failover plan (dedicated capacity fallback or region shift)

Customer update templates (practice variations):
- Initial: "We observed elevated latency impacting some calls. We're actively investigating the root cause and have engineers on it. We'll update within 15 minutes with next steps."
- After mitigation success: "We implemented a temporary routing change and are seeing p95 latency fall from 3.2s to ~0.8s. We will keep monitoring and follow up with a postmortem."
- If rollback/longer work required: "We will keep you updated with a targeted remediation ETA (approx 2–4 hours). We'll provide periodic updates every 30 minutes."

Dry-run scenarios to simulate (pick one):
A) Slow degradation after deployment (rollout-induced perf regression)
B) Sudden spike in request size causing KV cache thrash (high memory footprint)
C) Infra autoscaler misfire (delayed scale-up -> CPU/GPU saturation)

What to validate during the run:
- Can SRE trigger and observe a safe route change without breaking keys? (Maya + Omar)
- Does the customer message avoid technical blame and set realistic ETA? (Ravi + Iona)
- Are logs/trace ids captured for each step so postmortem can correlate? (scribe)

Playbook quick snippets (notes-to-self):
- If p95 > 2s and error rate > 1%: consider immediate route split to small-variant + increase cache TTLs.
- If GPU OOM flagged: check model token length distribution - ask customer for recent prompt examples.
- If autoscaler backoff: increase burst capacity (if account allows) or move traffic to dedicated pool in us-east (requires AM approval).

Known friction points to watch for (expected in dry-run):
- Confusion about who authorizes cross-region failover (IC must call out permission step).
- SE/Customer asks for ETA before we have instrumented metrics — practice safe language.
- Misaligned ownership for rollback scripts (repo: infra/rollouts) — confirm git/PR owner live.

Post-call action items (template — fill during real incident):
- Owner: Maya | Action: collect 1h of application logs + top 50 slow traces | Due: +2h | JIRA: NIM-3421
- Owner: Omar | Action: validate autoscaler logs + node health; snapshot node state | Due: +1h | JIRA: NIM-3421
- Owner: Ravi | Action: send customer interim update confirming mitigation and ETA | Due: immediate (within 15m)
- Owner: Iona | Action: schedule postmortem meeting and draft timeline | Due: same business day | JIRA: NIM-3421

Templates for scribe entries (quick):
- T+00:00 call opened by Iona, participants: Iona, Maya, Omar, Ravi
- T+00:03 identified symptom: p95 spike 3.2s, errors 2.1% (sample trace ids: abc123, def456)
- T+00:07 mitigation applied: route -> model-xsmall; observed p95 -> 0.9s after 2m
- T+00:15 customer updated by Ravi: sent initial + mitigation note

Unresolved questions / TODOs (for prep):
- Confirm whether Nimbus has private single-tenant pool that we can fail traffic to without billing impact; who signs off? (ask sales / contracts)
- Verify runbook permissions: can SRE trigger variant mapping without PR? (security check)
- Check if we have standard small-variant quantization profiles for every model family — if not, create ticket for pre-provisioning.

Final notes to self:
- Keep the dry-run low-risk: do not actually switch live traffic unless test flag ON or explicit "execute" from IC.
- Use this script to coach Ravi on concise customer updates (practice 2x).
- After dry-run, capture feedback in short retro: what took >2m, where did handoffs lag, any missing dashboards.

Quick retro prompts (post dry-run):
- What went well?
- What caused friction? (access, unclear roles, missing metrics)
- One improvement we will implement before next oncall: (e.g., pre-bake small-variant maps)

-----
Scratch: quick link stash for run (copy into bridge):
- Console routes: https://console.redwood.ai/routes/nimbus-prod
- Trace view: https://console.redwood.ai/traces?query=nimbus%20prod
- JIRA stub: https://jira.redwood.ai/browse/NIM-3421

(end of notes)
